title: Allowed outcome dependence increased maximum conditional errors by 44-45 percent in two ozone survival summaries from a 2024 extract
abstract: We tested how unknown outcome dependence changes conditional sampling uncertainty in two equal-paper ozone survival summaries. We held marginal delta variances fixed and allowed all positive semidefinite covariance matrices within each paper. Sharp maximum standard errors were 45.37 percent above the independence value for 34 survival-or-emergence records from nine papers, and 44.40 percent above it for 20 strict survival records from six papers. Both pooled independence ranges and maximum ranges included zero. A single later North American paper had an independence range below zero but a maximum range that included zero. Independent region and period tests were not supported. These are fixed-extract diagnostics, not population confidence intervals. Independent papers, valid marginal errors, effective sample sizes and independent treatment arms are required assumptions. Source selection, mixed endpoints, shared experiments and small samples limit interpretation. No climate interaction was tested. Code, aggregate results, source hashes and numerical checks are included.

display.caption: Fixed equal-paper log ratios with conditional 1.96 standard-error ranges. The maximum permits all within-paper dependence with fixed marginal errors and independent papers. Both pooled ranges include zero.
